research_basis: Fresh complete reviser synthesis of the admitted brief, investigator discovery/draft/source map/exact plan, critic critique/source map, and targeted independent primary-source rechecks. Source IDs S01-S13 are preserved without rebinding.

sources.title: Efficient Fair Queuing Using Deficit Round-Robin
sources.released_version_or_commit: IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking, vol. 4 no. 3, 1996
sources.locator: Title/abstract; article begins at p. 375; primary PDF landing/open
sources.observed_operation: Searched and opened the paper PDF; search-result excerpt exposed abstract and bibliographic details; PDF text extraction had no lines.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Authors describe DRR as an O(1) approximation for fair queuing in variable-length packet flows; applicability to task dispatch is an analogy, not a guarantee for memory or non-preemptive job workloads.
sources.applicability: Informs per-extension rotating dispatch and measured-cost fairness alternatives; does not directly specify desktop job scheduling.

sources.title: Control Group v2 — Linux kernel documentation
sources.released_version_or_commit: Linux kernel documentation tree 7.1; API behavior must be verified on supported installed kernels
sources.locator: Delegation section lines 174–179; memory interface lines 639–707; memory events lines 751–785
sources.observed_operation: Opened versioned kernel docs; inspected delegation model, memory.high/max, memory.current/peak and events.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Controller files are exposed only if controller is available/enabled; delegating access requires parent permissions; memory.high throttles and does not invoke OOM; memory.max is a hard limit that invokes cgroup OOM when reclaim fails, can temporarily be exceeded; major usage accounting is stated to be reasonable rather than fully watertight.
sources.applicability: Supports capability-gated Linux worker memory limits and event-based measurement; no-admin deployment can use only a writable pre-delegated cgroup. OOM action is scoped to cgroup per docs.

sources.title: JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION
sources.released_version_or_commit: Win32 desktop API; page shows minimum client Windows XP
sources.locator: Members ProcessMemoryLimit and JobMemoryLimit, lines 54–72 in opened documentation
sources.observed_operation: Opened API reference and inspected fields and remarks.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: PROCESS_MEMORY and JOB_MEMORY limits bound virtual memory that can be committed, not RSS/physical memory. Job and per-process commit limits are independent. Notification-limit path can notify while allowing further commits.
sources.applicability: Supports Windows task-descendant committed-memory boundary and calibration; UI must not equate commit cap with physical RAM cap.

sources.title: AssignProcessToJobObject
sources.released_version_or_commit: Win32 desktop API; nested-job behavior changed starting Windows 8 / Server 2012
sources.locator: Remarks on existing job, access rights, same session and older Windows versions; lines 51–70
sources.observed_operation: Opened API reference and inspected assignment constraints and OS-version exceptions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Assignment requires a job with assign rights and a process handle with quota/terminate rights. Already-jobbed processes must fit a valid nested hierarchy and cannot use UI limits; before Windows 8 the process could not already be in a job. All processes in a job must be in the same Terminal Services session.
sources.applicability: Requires launch-time capability probe; do not assume a worker can be added to a job in every host environment.

sources.title: Job Objects
sources.released_version_or_commit: Win32 Job Objects overview; nesting support Windows 8 / Server 2012 onward
sources.locator: Managing Job Objects lines 81–90, especially kill-on-job-close and nested process trees
sources.observed_operation: Opened overview and inspected handle-close cleanup and nesting conditions.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: If JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE is set, closing the last job handle terminates associated processes; nested jobs are available beginning Windows 8 and earlier systems need another process-tree strategy.
sources.applicability: Supports task-owned Windows worker cleanup after host crash and cancellation; exact outer-job compatibility remains a runtime check.

sources.title: Extension Host
sources.released_version_or_commit: VS Code docs, moving version; access 2026-10-12
sources.locator: Extension Host configurations and stability/performance section (official search excerpt; direct open timed out once)
sources.observed_operation: Searched official VS Code API docs; attempted direct open, which timed out; observed the official result excerpt.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: VS Code uses extension-host processes by runtime/location; docs position the host as separating extension execution from UI concerns. Multiple extensions may share a host; this is not per-task isolation.
sources.applicability: Illustrative separate extension-host architecture only; not evidence about the unnamed target application.

sources.title: VS Code Extension API — withProgress
sources.released_version_or_commit: VS Code API reference, current page; access 2026-10-12
sources.locator: window.withProgress reference, lines 2140–2150 in opened page
sources.observed_operation: Opened official API reference and read callback, progress increment and cancellation-token semantics.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Progress lifetime follows returned callback promise; only notification progress currently supports discrete progress and cancel button; task receives token to observe user cancellation. API describes signal delivery, not forced worker termination.
sources.applicability: Useful user-facing progress/cancel pattern; must be paired with host-owned cancellation and result-publication logic.

sources.title: VS Code extHostProgress.ts
sources.released_version_or_commit: Repository main branch, moving; commit SHA not exposed in fetched page; not release-pinned
sources.observed_operation: Opened current GitHub source page and inspected extension-host callback/token and cancellation bridge; GitHub showed branch main but no commit SHA.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: A CancellationTokenSource is created only for cancellable operations; callback receives its token; completion ends progress; incoming cancel calls source.cancel(). The task promise still controls completion, so no force-kill is implied.
sources.applicability: Concrete reference caller/implementation showing cooperative cancellation semantics in a real extension host, not target code.

sources.title: VS Code mainThreadProgress.ts
sources.released_version_or_commit: Repository main branch, moving; commit SHA not exposed in fetched page; not release-pinned
sources.locator: MainThreadProgress.$startProgress and cancellation callback, lines 444–479; extHostProgress token path, lines 487–535
sources.observed_operation: Opened current GitHub source page; read the main-thread progress listener that invokes $acceptProgressCanceled(handle), and the extension-host code that maps this to CancellationTokenSource.cancel(); the task promise still controls completion.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: UI cancellation crosses the extension-host/main-thread RPC bridge and signals a cooperative token. The implementation does not forcibly terminate a worker or provide durable job state; cancellation effectiveness depends on callback behavior.
sources.applicability: Reference for UI/process boundary only; not target app code.

sources.title: Test view-level progress from an extension (via withProgress API), issue #93822
sources.released_version_or_commit: Issue opened 2020-03-31; March 2020 milestone; closed testplan-item
sources.locator: Testing section lines 177–208; linked API declaration lines 183–208
sources.observed_operation: Opened official repository issue and read its test procedure.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: The issue asks a tester to create an extension/tree view and exercise view progress; it describes only Notification progress as currently offering cancel. It is a manual test-plan item, not a recorded test pass or fix.

sources.title: Write-Ahead Logging
sources.released_version_or_commit: SQLite current WAL documentation; access 2026-10-12; bug note lists release versions
sources.locator: WAL recovery and file behavior; section 11 WAL-reset bug, lines 191–195
sources.observed_operation: Opened official SQLite WAL documentation and inspected recovery, same-host caveat, retained WAL semantics, and release-fix note.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: WAL is part of persistent DB state and must travel with DB; WAL is same-host only; docs say a rare corruption bug affected 3.7.0 through 3.51.2 and is fixed in 3.51.3+ (backports 3.44.6 and 3.50.7), under simultaneous write/checkpoint conditions on multiple connections.
sources.applicability: If SQLite WAL is selected for durable job state, pin a fixed maintained release; see S12 for current release at research time. Not a requirement to adopt SQLite.

sources.title: SQLite Recent News — Version 3.54.0
sources.released_version_or_commit: SQLite 3.54.0 released 2026-10-09; news page as accessed 2026-10-12
sources.observed_operation: Opened official release/news page after checking current release history.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: Release entry states 3.54.0 includes enhancements and fixes; earlier 3.53.0 entry states WAL-reset fix and 3.51.3 entry lists patch fix. 3.54.0 is a current release, not a fixed promise of future support.
sources.applicability: Sets a date-bounded version reference if SQLite is chosen; verify the library actually shipped by the host application.

sources.title: SQLite is Transactional
sources.locator: Atomic/consistent/isolated/durable guarantee and regression-harness note, lines 20–28
sources.observed_operation: Opened official SQLite transaction page and read ACID/crash guarantee and test-harness statement.
sources.governing_condition_default_exception: SQLite states a single transaction is all-or-none through program, OS, or power failure and says this is extensively checked by a special crash/power-loss harness; actual durability still depends on selected SQLite configuration and storage behavior.
sources.applicability: Supports a local state journal option and fault-injection validation proposal; does not make journal and report files one atomic transaction.

reviewer_checks.locator: Delegation at lines 174-180; cgroup fork/migration at 80-86; memory accounting at 639-650; memory.high/max at 683-707
reviewer_checks.observed_operation: Opened versioned kernel documentation and checked delegation permissions, process inheritance/migration, memory.high, memory.max, and accounting caveat.
reviewer_checks.governing_condition_default_exception: Children fork into the parent's current cgroup; moving a process does not move existing descendants. memory.high throttles/reclaims and does not invoke OOM; memory.max is a hard limit that may be temporarily exceeded and invokes cgroup OOM when reclaim cannot meet it. Available controllers and delegation depend on system configuration and parent permissions.
reviewer_checks.applicability: Confirms predecessor caveats and supplies the launch-containment condition for MI-2.

reviewer_checks.locator: ProcessMemoryLimit and JobMemoryLimit members and remarks
reviewer_checks.observed_operation: Opened primary Microsoft Learn API result and checked committed-virtual-memory semantics, independent process/job limits, and peak accounting.
reviewer_checks.governing_condition_default_exception: Limits apply only when corresponding flags are set; process and job limits are independent; they are not physical RSS caps.
reviewer_checks.applicability: Confirms the draft's Windows UI must call this a commit-memory boundary, not a physical-RAM cap.

reviewer_checks.observed_operation: Opened the primary Microsoft Learn function reference and checked handle rights, same-session and nested-job conditions, pre-Windows-8 behavior, and child/breakaway behavior.
reviewer_checks.governing_condition_default_exception: Assignment requires job/process rights; an already-jobbed process must fit nested-job conditions; older Windows versions reject already-jobbed processes; children ordinarily inherit job membership but breakaway flags and job settings matter.
reviewer_checks.applicability: Confirms capability probing and the additional MI-2 requirement to prevent or detect boundary escape.

reviewer_checks.locator: Closing job handles and managing process trees
reviewer_checks.observed_operation: Opened the primary Job Objects overview and checked kill-on-last-handle behavior and nested-job version boundary.
reviewer_checks.governing_condition_default_exception: Kill-on-close applies when the last job handle closes; nested jobs are available beginning Windows 8 / Windows Server 2012.
reviewer_checks.applicability: Confirms the draft's task-owned Windows cleanup caveat.

reviewer_checks.governing_condition_default_exception: Progress is shown while callback promise remains unsettled; the token signals cancellation; only Notification currently supports discrete progress and cancel button.

reviewer_checks.governing_condition_default_exception: UI progress cancellation signals the extension-host cancellation source; task termination is not implemented by this bridge. Moving main branch; no release SHA established here.

reviewer_checks.observed_operation: Opened official GitHub issue and confirmed testplan-item label, manual view-progress procedure, and closed-completed status.

reviewer_checks.locator: Atomic transaction/crash behavior and test-harness note, lines 20-28

reviewer_checks.governing_condition_default_exception: Guarantee covers changes within one SQLite transaction; it does not join external filesystems or report artifacts into that transaction.
reviewer_checks.applicability: Supports a possible local journal, not cross-resource atomic publication.

reviser_checks.title: Control Group v2 — Linux kernel documentation
reviser_checks.released_version_or_commit: Linux kernel documentation tree 7.1; behavior must be verified on supported installed kernels
reviser_checks.locator: Process organization lines 20-23 and 83-86; controller availability lines 145-157; delegation lines 174-204; memory accounting lines 639-650; memory.high/max and events lines 683-785
reviser_checks.observed_operation: Independently reopened the versioned primary kernel documentation and inspected process placement, migration, delegation, memory accounting, memory.high, memory.max, and memory events. It states children enter the parent's current cgroup, later migration does not move existing descendants, and recommends assigning at startup. A second direct open returned the same primary page.
reviser_checks.governing_condition_default_exception: Controller availability and delegation depend on configuration and permissions. memory.high throttles/reclaims, never invokes OOM itself, and may be breached; memory.max is the hard cgroup limit, may be temporarily exceeded, and can invoke OOM within the cgroup. Major memory accounting is not completely watertight.
reviser_checks.applicability: Rechecks MI-1 fallback and MI-2 launch containment. Supports placing the worker in its task cgroup before extension code can fork; no-admin hard control exists only where a writable delegation is already available.

reviser_checks.title: JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION
reviser_checks.released_version_or_commit: Win32 desktop API reference; page lists minimum client Windows XP and last updated 2021-04-02
reviser_checks.locator: ProcessMemoryLimit and JobMemoryLimit members and remarks, lines 54-72
reviser_checks.observed_operation: Opened the primary Microsoft Learn result and read the memory-limit member definitions and remarks; a later direct reload returned an internal error, so the successful search/open content is the basis of this check.
reviser_checks.governing_condition_default_exception: Limits apply only when the corresponding JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT flags are set; process and job limits are independent and bound virtual memory that can be committed, not RSS or physical RAM. Notification limits may report while allowing further commits.
reviser_checks.applicability: Rechecks MI-1 capability-specific override and prevents the UI from calling the Windows boundary a physical-RAM cap.

reviser_checks.title: AssignProcessToJobObject
reviser_checks.released_version_or_commit: Win32 desktop API reference; page last updated 2021-10-13; nested-job behavior changed starting Windows 8 / Server 2012
reviser_checks.locator: Parameters and Remarks, especially access rights, already-jobbed/nesting and OS-version conditions, pre-assignment memory, and child inheritance/breakaway, lines 48-72
reviser_checks.observed_operation: Found the official Microsoft Learn function page through primary-source search and opened it. Checked assignment rights, nesting/OS-version conditions, pre-assignment memory behavior, and default child association/breakaway. A later direct reload returned an internal error; the successful official page text is retained.
reviser_checks.governing_condition_default_exception: Assignment requires appropriate job/process rights. Already-jobbed processes must fit nested-job constraints; older systems reject already-jobbed processes. Memory activity before assignment is not examined. Children normally inherit job association, except when breakaway is allowed/requested; nested settings matter.
reviser_checks.applicability: Rechecks MI-2. Requires an inert/suspended worker and verified job assignment/limits before extension code is released; assignment failure cannot be described as a hard boundary.

reviser_checks.title: Job Objects
reviser_checks.released_version_or_commit: Win32 Job Objects documentation; page last updated 2025-07-14; nested jobs begin Windows 8 / Server 2012
reviser_checks.locator: Managing Processes in Jobs and Managing a Process Tree; child-process inheritance, breakaway flags, IsProcessInJob, kill-on-last-handle behavior
reviser_checks.observed_operation: Opened the primary Microsoft Learn Job Objects page and checked child association, breakaway configurations, nested-job constraints, and kill-on-close. A later direct reload returned an internal error; the successful official search result/open content is the basis of this check.
reviser_checks.governing_condition_default_exception: CreateProcess children inherit membership by default, but breakaway flags/job settings can change this and Win32_Process.Create children are not associated by default. Kill-on-close requires the last job handle to close. Job nesting differs on older Windows.
reviser_checks.applicability: Rechecks MI-2 boundary and cleanup. A hard descendant guarantee requires a verified configuration and controlled child-launch paths; Job Objects are not a general extension security sandbox.
